	window.StarlightThemeProvider = (() => {
		const storedTheme =
			typeof localStorage !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem('starlight-theme');
		const theme =
			storedTheme ||
			(window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? 'light' : 'dark');
		document.documentElement.dataset.theme = theme === 'light' ? 'light' : 'dark';
		return {
			updatePickers(theme = storedTheme || 'auto') {
				document.querySelectorAll('starlight-theme-select').forEach((picker) => {
					const select = picker.querySelector('select');
					if (select) select.value = theme;
					/** @type {HTMLTemplateElement | null} */
					const tmpl = document.querySelector(`#theme-icons`);
					const newIcon = tmpl && tmpl.content.querySelector('.' + theme);
					if (newIcon) {
						const oldIcon = picker.querySelector('svg.label-icon');
						if (oldIcon) {
							oldIcon.replaceChildren(...newIcon.cloneNode(true).childNodes);
						}
					}
				});
			},
		};
	})();

<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h2"><h2 id="remarks">Remarks</h2><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#remarks"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “Remarks”</span></a></div>
<p><code dir="auto">core:window:default</code> only enables the getters (sizes, positions,
monitors, title, theme and the <code dir="auto">is*</code> queries). Creating a window and every
method that changes one needs its own permission, which each member documents,
added to a capability in your app.</p>

<p>Prevents the window from being closed.</p>
<p>Must be called before the handler returns (await anything you need first),
otherwise the window is destroyed as usual.</p>

<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h3"><h3 id="window">Window</h3><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#window"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “Window”</span></a></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L377">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L377</a></p>
<p>Create new window or get a handle to an existing one.</p>
<p>Windows are identified by a <em>label</em>  a unique identifier that can be used to reference it later.
It may only contain alphanumeric characters <code dir="auto">a-zA-Z</code> plus the following special characters <code dir="auto">-</code>, <code dir="auto">/</code>, <code dir="auto">:</code> and <code dir="auto">_</code>.</p>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">activityName</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">(): </span><span style="--0:#C5E478;--1:#3B61B0">Promise</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">string</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&gt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="activityName(): Promise<string>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L965">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L965</a></p>
<p>The name of the Android activity hosting this window.</p>
<p>On Android each window is backed by its own activity. Use this to tell windows
apart from native code, or to match a window with the activity declared in your
<code dir="auto">AndroidManifest.xml</code>.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Android:</strong> Supported.</li>
<li><strong>Windows / Linux / macOS / iOS:</strong> Unsupported, the call rejects because the
command is not registered.</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="https://tauri.app/learn/mobile-multiwindow/">mobile multiwindow guide</a>.</p>

<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h6"><h6 id="remarks-8">Remarks</h6><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#remarks-8"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “Remarks”</span></a></div>
<p>The listener is removed automatically when this window is destroyed,
so you do not need to unlisten just because the window is closing. Do call the
returned function when the listener’s own scope ends, e.g. on page navigation
or when a component unmounts.</p>

automatically when this window is destroyed. Do call the returned function if

<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h6"><h6 id="remarks-12">Remarks</h6><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#remarks-12"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “Remarks”</span></a></div>
<p>The listener is removed automatically when this window is destroyed,
so you do not need to unlisten just because the window is closing. Do call the
returned function when the listener’s own scope ends, e.g. on page navigation
or when a component unmounts.</p>
<p><a id="ondragdropevent"></a></p>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L2407">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L2407</a></p>
<p>Listen to a file drop event.
The listener is triggered when the user hovers the selected files on the webview,
drops the files or cancels the operation.</p>

<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h6"><h6 id="remarks-13">Remarks</h6><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#remarks-13"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “Remarks”</span></a></div>
<p>The listener is removed automatically when this window is destroyed,
so you do not need to unlisten just because the window is closing. Do call the
returned function when the listener’s own scope ends, e.g. on page navigation
or when a component unmounts.</p>

<p>The listener is removed automatically when this window is destroyed,
so you do not need to unlisten just because the window is closing. Do call the
returned function when the listener’s own scope ends, e.g. on page navigation
or when a component unmounts.</p>

<p>Listen to window scale change. Emitted when the window’s scale factor has changed.
The following user actions can cause DPI changes:</p>
<ul>
<li>Changing the display’s resolution.</li>
<li>Changing the display’s scale factor (e.g. in Control Panel on Windows).</li>
<li>Moving the window to a display with a different scale factor.</li>
</ul>

<p>The listener is removed automatically when this window is destroyed,
so you do not need to unlisten just because the window is closing. Do call the
returned function when the listener’s own scope ends, e.g. on page navigation
or when a component unmounts.</p>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">requestUserAttention</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">(requestType): </span><span style="--0:#C5E478;--1:#3B61B0">Promise</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#7FDBCA;--1:#096E72">void</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&gt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="requestUserAttention(requestType): Promise<void>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1049">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1049</a></p>
<p>Requests user attention to the window, this has no effect if the application
is already focused. How requesting for user attention manifests is platform dependent,
see <code dir="auto">UserAttentionType</code> for details.</p>
<p>Providing <code dir="auto">null</code> will unset the request for user attention. Unsetting the request for
user attention might not be done automatically by the WM when the window receives input.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>macOS:</strong> <code dir="auto">null</code> has no effect.</li>
<li><strong>Linux:</strong> Urgency levels have the same effect.</li>
</ul>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">sceneIdentifier</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">(): </span><span style="--0:#C5E478;--1:#3B61B0">Promise</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">string</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&gt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="sceneIdentifier(): Promise<string>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L999">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L999</a></p>
<p>The identifier of the iOS scene hosting this window.</p>
<p>On iOS each window is backed by a <code dir="auto">UIScene</code>. Use this to tell windows apart
from native code, or to match a window with a scene configuration declared in
your <code dir="auto">Info.plist</code>.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>iOS:</strong> Supported.</li>
<li><strong>Windows / Linux / macOS / Android:</strong> Unsupported, the call rejects because
the command is not registered.</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="https://tauri.app/learn/mobile-multiwindow/">mobile multiwindow guide</a>.</p>

<p>Sets the window background color.</p>
<p>Platform-specific:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Windows:</strong> alpha channel is ignored.</li>
<li><strong>iOS / Android:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
</ul>
<p>This sets the color of the window itself, which is what you see while the
webview is still loading or behind a transparent page. To also change the
webview background use <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewebviewwindow/#setbackgroundcolor">WebviewWindow.setBackgroundColor</a>.</p>

<p>Sets the badge label shown on the app’s dock icon. <strong>macOS only</strong></p>
<p>Unlike <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setbadgecount"><code dir="auto">Window.setBadgeCount</code></a>, which takes a number, this shows
arbitrary short text. It is app-wide and not specific to this window.</p>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1201">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1201</a></p>
<p>Sets whether the window’s native close button is enabled or not.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Linux:</strong> GTK+ will do its best to convince the window manager not to show a close button. Depending on the system, this function may not have any effect when called on a window that is already visible</li>

<p>Grabs the cursor, preventing it from leaving the window.</p>
<p>There’s no guarantee that the cursor will be hidden. You should
hide it by yourself if you want so.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Linux:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
<li><strong>macOS:</strong> This locks the cursor in a fixed location, which looks visually awkward.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1929">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1929</a></p>
<p>Modifies the cursor’s visibility.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Windows:</strong> The cursor is only hidden within the confines of the window.</li>
<li><strong>macOS:</strong> The cursor is hidden as long as the window has input focus, even if the cursor is
outside of the window.</li>
</ul>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">setEffects</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">(effects): </span><span style="--0:#C5E478;--1:#3B61B0">Promise</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#7FDBCA;--1:#096E72">void</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&gt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="setEffects(effects): Promise<void>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1489">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1489</a></p>
<p>Applies platform-specific window effects such as Mica, Acrylic, Blur or the
macOS vibrancy materials.</p>
<p>Requires the window to be transparent, so create it with <code dir="auto">transparent: true</code>
(or set <code dir="auto">transparent</code> in <code dir="auto">tauri.conf.json</code>). Give the page a transparent or
translucent background as well, otherwise the effect is hidden behind your own
background color.</p>
<p>Conflicting effects are resolved by applying the first supported one and
ignoring the rest, so you can list a Windows and a macOS effect together.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Windows:</strong> If the window uses decorations or shadows, you may need
<a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tao/issues/72#issuecomment-975607891">this workaround</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Linux:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1820">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1820</a></p>
<p>Sets whether the window can be focused.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>macOS</strong>: If the window is already focused, it is not possible to unfocus it after calling <code dir="auto">set_focusable(false)</code>.
In this case, you might consider calling <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setfocus">Window.setFocus</a> but it will move the window to the back i.e. at the bottom in terms of z-order.</li>
</ul>

<p>Sets whether the window’s native maximize button is enabled or not.
If resizable is set to false, this setting is ignored.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>macOS:</strong> Disables the “zoom” button in the window titlebar, which is also used to enter fullscreen mode.</li>
<li><strong>Linux / iOS / Android:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
</ul>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1445">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1445</a></p>
<p>Whether or not the window should have shadow.</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Windows:</strong>
<ul>
<li><code dir="auto">false</code> has no effect on decorated window, shadows are always ON.</li>
<li><code dir="auto">true</code> will make undecorated window have a 1px white border,
and on Windows 11, it will have a rounded corners.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Linux:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
</ul>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">setSimpleFullscreen</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">(fullscreen): </span><span style="--0:#C5E478;--1:#3B61B0">Promise</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#7FDBCA;--1:#096E72">void</span><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">&gt;</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="setSimpleFullscreen(fullscreen): Promise<void>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1774">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L1774</a></p>
<p>On macOS, Toggles a fullscreen mode that doesn’t require a new macOS space. Returns a boolean indicating whether the transition was successful (this won’t work if the window was already in the native fullscreen).
This is how fullscreen used to work on macOS in versions before Lion. And allows the user to have a fullscreen window without using another space or taking control over the entire monitor.</p>
<p>On other platforms, this is the same as <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setfullscreen">Window.setFullscreen</a>.</p>

<p>Set window theme, pass in <code dir="auto">null</code> or <code dir="auto">undefined</code> to follow system theme</p>
<p>Platform-specific</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Linux / macOS</strong>: Theme is app-wide and not specific to this window.</li>
<li><strong>iOS / Android:</strong> Unsupported.</li>
</ul>
<p>Use <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#theme">Window.theme</a> to read the effective theme and
<a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#onthemechanged">Window.onThemeChanged</a> to react to changes.</p>

<p>Sets the title bar style. <strong>macOS only</strong>.</p>
<p>Use <code dir="auto">transparent</code> or <code dir="auto">overlay</code> to build a custom title bar: with <code dir="auto">overlay</code> the
page extends under the title bar and only the traffic lights remain, so leave
room for them in your layout and pair it with <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#startdragging">Window.startDragging</a> on a
draggable region.</p>

<td><a id="parent"></a> <code dir="auto">parent?</code></td>
<td>| <code dir="auto">string</code> | <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#window"><code dir="auto">Window</code></a> | <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewebviewwindow/#webviewwindow"><code dir="auto">WebviewWindow</code></a></td>
<td>Sets a parent to the window to be created. Can be either a <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#window"><code dir="auto">Window</code></a> or a label of the window. Platform-specific - <strong>Windows</strong>: This sets the passed parent as an owner window to the window to be created. From <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-features#owned-windows">MSDN owned windows docs</a>: - An owned window is always above its owner in the z-order. - The system automatically destroys an owned window when its owner is destroyed. - An owned window is hidden when its owner is minimized. - <strong>Linux</strong>: This makes the new window transient for parent, see <a href="https://docs.gtk.org/gtk3/method.Window.set_transient_for.html">https://docs.gtk.org/gtk3/method.Window.set_transient_for.html</a> - <strong>macOS</strong>: This adds the window as a child of parent, see <a href="https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/1419152-addchildwindow?language=objc">https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/1419152-addchildwindow?language=objc</a></td>
<td><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L2977">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L2977</a></td>

<p><a id="windowsizeconstraints"></a></p>
<div class="sl-heading-wrapper level-h3"><h3 id="windowsizeconstraints">WindowSizeConstraints</h3><a class="sl-anchor-link" href="#windowsizeconstraints"><span aria-hidden="true" class="sl-anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor"><path d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42m8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42 1 1 0 0 0 1.42 0l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33M8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 .71.29 1 1 0 0 0 .71-.29l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42"></path></svg></span><span class="sr-only" data-pagefind-ignore>Section titled “WindowSizeConstraints”</span></a></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L284">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L284</a></p>
<p>Inner size constraints for a window, see <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setsizeconstraints">Window.setSizeConstraints</a>.</p>
<p>Unlike <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setminsize">Window.setMinSize</a> and <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setmaxsize">Window.setMaxSize</a>, each dimension is
independent: you can constrain only the width and leave the height free.</p>
<p>All values are in <strong>logical pixels</strong>. Leave a field out (or set it to
<code dir="auto">undefined</code>) to remove that constraint.</p>

<p>The cursor shape to display over a window, see <a href="/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/#setcursoricon">Window.setCursorIcon</a>.</p>
<p>The names mirror the CSS <code dir="auto">cursor</code> keywords in camelCase (e.g. <code dir="auto">notAllowed</code> for
<code dir="auto">not-allowed</code>, <code dir="auto">eResize</code> for <code dir="auto">e-resize</code>). Support varies per platform and window
manager; unsupported values fall back to the default arrow.</p>

<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L111">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L111</a></p>
<p>The style of the window title bar. <strong>macOS only</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code dir="auto">visible</code>: the standard title bar.</li>
<li><code dir="auto">transparent</code>: the title bar is transparent but the traffic lights stay in place.</li>
<li><code dir="auto">overlay</code>: the content extends under a transparent title bar, leaving only the
traffic lights visible.</li>
</ul>

<div class="expressive-code"><figure class="frame not-content"><figcaption class="header"></figcaption><pre data-language="ts"><code><div class="ec-line"><div class="code"><span style="--0:#C792EA;--1:#8844AE">function</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53"> </span><span style="--0:#82AAFF;--1:#3B61B0">cursorPosition</span><span style="--0:#D9F5DD;--1:#111111">()</span><span style="--0:#7FDBCA;--1:#096E72">:</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53"> </span><span style="--0:#FFCB8B;--1:#111111">Promise</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">&lt;</span><span style="--0:#FFCB8B;--1:#111111">PhysicalPosition</span><span style="--0:#D6DEEB;--1:#403F53">&gt;;</span></div></div></code></pre><div class="copy"><div aria-live="polite"></div><button title="Copy to clipboard" data-copied="Copied!" data-code="function cursorPosition(): Promise<PhysicalPosition>;"><div></div></button></div></figure></div>
<p><strong>Source</strong>: <a href="https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L3179">https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/packages/api/src/window.ts#L3179</a></p>
<p>Get the cursor position relative to the top-left hand corner of the desktop.</p>
<p>Note that the top-left hand corner of the desktop is not necessarily the same as the screen.
If the user uses a desktop with multiple monitors,
the top-left hand corner of the desktop is the top-left hand corner of the main monitor on Windows and macOS
or the top-left of the leftmost monitor on X11.</p>
<p>The coordinates can be negative if the top-left hand corner of the window is outside of the visible screen region.</p>
